kind: read-only source audit; no test execution or retry
head: 7842205f1e7b85466b6f2fd9b613ef127df1aa39

application_result.error: My skills did not answer in time.

retained_observation.limits: No call ordinal, per-call elapsed value, enqueue/dequeue/commit timestamps, scheduling trace or filesystem duration was retained. The diagnostic is not itself a measured 1 s timeout. No binary drift or host-load cause is established.

startup_order.fact: Create waking ToolAsk channel, then listen() binds call.sock and spawns the serial listener. listen() does not publish tools.json.
First main-loop reload scans assets, fingerprints and loads the four fixture skills, replaces Engine and permissions. This work precedes initial registry publication.
write_tools publishes tools.json by temporary write and rename (2774-2785), before bus subscriber setup. Registry existence is not an acknowledgement that the main request queue is being serviced.

Build topic list, create missing subscriptions through 1209, check tool socket at 1212, refresh publisher liveness at 1214, then clock/routine/Engine work before wait_any at 1278 and first asks.try_recv at 1293.

Each new subscription synchronously reads declaration, creates directories, binds, chmods, hard-links and unlinks a Unix socket (190-239), then allocates a 60,001-byte buffer at 258. No deadline wraps that filesystem work.

timeout_and_reply.fact: TOOL_TIMEOUT is 1 s. Listener sends ToolAsk then waits at 2976; timeout/disconnection cancels admission when still pending, otherwise waits another 1 s. A missing result produces the observed error at 2987. Invalid requests or failed channel send also share this generic error; this fixture sends a valid wave call.

Admission uses atomic PENDING -> COMMITTED or CANCELLED. A cancellation that wins prevents later tool_call commit (main 2700-2703). This is a cancellation bound, not evidence of where the failed run waited.
The fixture wave has only Say. It sends the reply at 2714 before publishing Triggered/Done events. No Actions/Mood/provider connection or look-readiness wait is required for that response.

Fixture waits only for tools.json existence, then sleeps 30 ms before each of 10 sequential calls. The first response assertion fails before printing durations or evaluating median 25 ms; the failed ordinal is not recorded.

other_main_thread_work.fact: Sending a ToolAsk queues it then writes a nonblocking wake pipe. wait_any polls all topics plus that pipe once (640-710); WAIT_AT_MOST is 250 ms. Even wake-error fallback sleeps only the remaining 250 ms; it does not intentionally wait 250 ms for each topic. Scheduling suspension can exceed requested waits, but no such suspension is measured here.

Every 2 s the same main loop fingerprints the skills tree and performs reload checks before draining asks (1075-1214). Normal filesystem calls have no wall-time limit; a slow scan can delay already-queued calls even after startup.

After replying, Triggered/Done event publication may synchronously scan subscribers/refresh presence (bus/publish.rs646-680,713-740). Later calls can queue behind this work. The isolated fixture has no event subscribers, so ordinary work is small; no long duration was observed.

Between call-drain passes, each subscriber recv(Duration::ZERO) uses a nonblocking socket but can check retained latest files (bus/subscribe.rs611-617,759-772; wire.rs166-177). Fixture creates an otherwise empty private bus. No retained-message flood is established.

Fixture provides no zone/offset, so sample_clock performs no time-zone/synchronization lookup; it has no clock trigger, watch, requested-audio asset or look. Initial state/known/daily setup precedes registry publication. The retained environment receipt lists build/test variables only and is not a complete inherited runtime-switch inventory.

assessment.established_source_exposure: tools.json becomes visible before subscription construction and main-loop request service; synchronous filesystem work is also interleaved with subsequent requests. Both can consume the listener deadline if they stall.
assessment.not_established: No deterministic 1 s stall, broken wake, dropped handle, changes-trigger regression, deadlock, device/provider wait or attribution to startup was demonstrated. Source-only review cannot assign this particular failure to I/O or scheduling. Missing Triggered lines are insufficient to identify the first failed call because the process uses a dropping log relay and the fixture kills it on panic.
assessment.disposition: Preserve first failure as unresolved. No timeout change, test retry or product correction performed.

bounded_next_diagnostic_not_run: Record call ordinal and monotonic boundaries for registry rename, end of subscriptions/startup, ToolAsk enqueue, dequeue, admission commit and reply reception; retain independent I/O durations or a main-thread sample if a stall occurs. A controlled post-registry startup-work barrier would test readiness ordering without increasing the 1 s product timeout or the 25 ms response target. Moving registry publication after startup work would narrow only the startup exposure; it would not resolve periodic filesystem stalls.
scope_limits: No source/test edits, builds, Cargo, reruns, device access, network calls or public posts. The separate Tests-owned Routine 50 ms investigation is untouched.
